examples.en: The violin and cello are string instruments.
I took a string instrument part in the school orchestra.
String instruments sound soft.
Among string instruments, I like the cello best.
The gayageum is a typical Korean string instrument.
This piece is played with only string instruments.

explain: 줄이 있는 악기를 모두 부르는 말이에요. 부는 악기는 '관악기', 치는 악기는 '타악기'로 짝을 이뤄 외우면 좋아요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 바이올린은 '켜다', 가야금은 '타다', 기타는 '치다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I have played string instruments since I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기 이름 대신 현악기 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to speak of string instruments in general, not one by name.

phrases.en: The sound of string instruments is soft, so I feel relaxed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄을 울려서 나는 소리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sound made by vibrating strings.

phrases.en: Among string instruments, I like the cello best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 줄 악기 가운데 하나를 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to pick one out of several string instruments.

explain_en: It pairs with '관악기' (wind) and '타악기' (percussion). Each instrument takes its own verb: '켜다' for the violin, '타다' for the gayageum, and '치다' for the guitar.

examples.en: We caught clams on the tidal flat of the West Sea.
When the water goes out, the mud flat is exposed widely.
The kids took off their shoes and walked on the mud flat.
You need to book the mud flat experience for the weekend.

examples.ko: 갯벌에는 게와 작은 생물이 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many crabs and small creatures live on tidal flats.
I woke up early to take photos of the tidal flat.

explain: '해변'은 모래가 있는 바닷가이고, 갯벌은 진흙이 넓게 펼쳐진 곳이에요. 밀물과 썰물 때문에 하루에 두 번 모습이 바뀌어서, 가기 전에 물때를 확인해야 해요. 서해안에 특히 넓어요.

phrases.en: On the weekend, I did a mudflat experience program with the kids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갯벌에서 조개를 잡거나 걷는 관광 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tourist activity like digging for clams or walking on the flat.

phrases.en: I checked the tide and went to the tidal flat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 말할 때 '에'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 에 for the place you go to.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the tidal flat

phrases.en: Walking on the tidal flat barefoot feels special.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진흙 위를 걷는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means walking on the muddy ground.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk on the tidal flat

explain_en: 해변 is a sandy shore, while 갯벌 is a wide stretch of mud. The tide changes it twice a day, so check the tide times (물때) before you go. The west coast has especially big ones.

examples.en: A honeybee is flying around over the flowers.

examples.ko: 꿀벌 덕분에 우리가 맛있는 꿀을 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to honeybees, we can eat delicious honey.
When spring comes, honeybees work busily.
My grandfather raises honeybees in the mountains.
Many people are worried because honeybees are decreasing.
The child colored the honeybee drawing yellow.

explain: 꿀벌은 꿀을 모으는 벌이에요. 그냥 '벌'은 쏘는 벌 전체를 가리키는 넓은 말이고, 꿀벌은 그 가운데 꿀을 만드는 종류예요. 부지런히 일하는 사람을 '꿀벌처럼 일한다'고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: He works nonstop like a honeybee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부지런히 일하는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison for someone who works diligently.

phrases.example: 꿀벌 한 마리가 창문 안으로 들어왔어요.
phrases.en: A honeybee came in through the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌레나 동물은 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Insects and animals are counted with 마리.

phrases.en: Honeybees collect honey from flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿀벌이 하는 가장 대표적인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the most typical thing honeybees do.

explain_en: 꿀벌 is the bee that gathers honey. Plain 벌 is the broad word for stinging insects of this kind, and 꿀벌 is the type among them that makes honey. Koreans may also say someone works 꿀벌처럼 to praise a diligent worker.

examples.en: While traveling, I felt the beauty of nature.
In front of grand nature, people look small.
I want to rest for a few days in the great outdoors.
This movie was shot against a backdrop of vast nature.
Feel the peace that nature gives.
We are a part of nature.

explain: 그냥 '자연'보다 크고 웅장한 느낌이에요. 산, 바다, 사막처럼 넓은 자연을 말할 때 어울려요. 말할 때보다 글이나 여행 이야기에서 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain and saw the beauty of nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자연의 크고 멋진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the grand, impressive look of nature.

phrases.en: I spent a day out in the wilds of nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 자연 안에 있는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes being inside vast nature.

phrases.en: I could feel the greatness of nature on the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행이나 감상을 이야기할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suits talking about travel or impressions.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel the grandeur of nature

explain_en: It feels bigger and more majestic than plain '자연'. It suits wide landscapes such as mountains, seas and deserts. It fits writing and travel stories better than casual talk.

examples.en: A lizard is clinging to the wall.
My younger brother wants to keep a lizard.
A lizard cuts off its tail when in danger.
I saw a big lizard at the zoo.
It ran away fast like a lizard.
The lizard basking in the sun was cute.

explain: '뱀'과 이름이 비슷하지만 다리가 있고 꼬리가 끊어졌다가 다시 자라요. 그래서 '도마뱀 꼬리 자르기'는 윗사람이 책임을 아랫사람에게 넘길 때 비유로 써요. '도롱뇽'과는 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 윗사람이 책임을 피하려고 도마뱀 꼬리 자르기를 했다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: cutting off the lizard's tail (sacrificing a subordinate)
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생겼을 때 윗사람이 아랫사람만 책임지게 하고 빠져나갈 때 비유로 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for a superior sacrificing a subordinate to escape blame when something goes wrong. Often heard in the news.
phrases.en_equiv: make a scapegoat of a subordinate

explain_en: The name looks like 뱀 (snake), but a 도마뱀 has legs and can regrow a tail that it sheds. The saying 도마뱀 꼬리 자르기 (cutting off the lizard's tail) is used when someone in charge pushes blame onto someone lower. It is a different animal from 도롱뇽 (salamander).

examples.ko: 길가에 이름 모를 들꽃이 피어 있어요.
examples.en: Wildflowers whose names I don't know are blooming by the road.
Don't pick wildflowers, just look at them.

examples.ko: 봄이 오면 들꽃 구경하러 산에 가요.
examples.en: When spring comes, I go to the mountains to see wildflowers.
Even one small wildflower makes my mind feel at ease.

examples.ko: 들꽃은 화단의 꽃보다 더 강해 보여요.
examples.en: Wildflowers look tougher than flowers in a flower bed.
The children made flower rings out of wildflowers.

explain: 사람이 가꾸지 않아도 산과 들에서 저절로 피는 꽃이에요. 반대로 사람이 심고 가꾸는 꽃은 '화초'라고 해요.

phrases.en: When spring comes, wild flowers bloom along the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 바뀌어 꽃이 필 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for flowers blooming as the seasons change.

phrases.en: I found a single wild flower on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 셀 때는 '송이'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 송이 as the counter for flowers.

phrases.en: I took photos of wild flowers in the park on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들꽃은 사진이나 그림의 소재로 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wild flowers are a popular subject for photos and drawings.

explain_en: Everyday word for flowers growing in fields and paths. These are flowers that bloom on their own in mountains and fields without anyone tending them. Flowers that people plant and care for are called '화초'.

t90.ax: Don't pick wildflowers, just look at them.

examples.en: I scraped the fish scales off with a knife.
The fish's scales sparkle in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 뱀의 몸은 단단한 비늘로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: A snake's body is covered with tough scales.

examples.ko: 생선을 사 오면 먼저 비늘 손질부터 해요.
examples.en: When I bring fish home, I start by dealing with the scales.
Fish with lots of scales are hard to prepare.

examples.ko: 용 그림에는 번쩍이는 비늘이 아주 많이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: The dragon painting has a great many shiny scales drawn on it.

explain: 물고기나 뱀, 용처럼 몸이 작은 조각으로 덮인 동물에 써요. 새의 '깃털', 동물의 '털'과는 다른 말이에요. 요리 전에는 '비늘을 벗기다', '비늘을 긁다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I scaled the fish before cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 비늘을 없애는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to removing scales when preparing fish.

phrases.en: The fish's scales sparkle in the sunlight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비늘이 빛나는 모습을 묘사할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe scales shining.

phrases.en: Snake scales are hard and smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물고기 말고 뱀에게도 비늘이 있다는 것을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that snakes, not only fish, have 비늘.

explain_en: Scales of fish or reptiles; cooking, nature. It is for animals like fish, snakes, and dragons whose bodies are covered in small plates. It is different from '깃털' (bird feathers) and '털' (fur). Before cooking, people say '비늘을 벗기다' or '비늘을 긁다'.

t90.ax: The fish's scales sparkle in the sunlight.

examples.en: This year every fruit tree is heavy with fruit.

examples.ko: 포도가 주렁주렁 달린 모습이 정말 풍성해요.
examples.en: The sight of grapes hanging in bunches looks really abundant.
She carries a bag with lots of dolls dangling from it.

examples.ko: 크리스마스 트리에 장식이 주렁주렁 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: Decorations hang all over the Christmas tree.
Persimmons hang in clusters on the persimmon tree.
If you pile on necklaces, it actually looks awkward.

explain: 열매나 장식 같은 것이 많이 매달려 있는 모양을 말해요. '대롱대롱'은 한두 개가 가볍게 매달린 모양이라 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: Persimmons hang in clusters on the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열매가 많이 붙어 있는 모습을 말할 때 가장 흔히 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for fruit hanging abundantly.

phrases.en: Tomatoes grew in abundance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달리다'보다 열매가 맺힌다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of fruit forming and growing than 달리다.

phrases.en: Lots of dolls are dangling from the bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열매뿐 아니라 장식이나 물건이 많이 매달린 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works not only for fruit but also for many decorations or items dangling.

explain_en: Many fruits or items hanging down in clusters. It describes many things such as fruit or decorations hanging down together. '대롱대롱' is different, since it describes one or a few things dangling lightly.

examples.en: The chameleon is famous as an animal that changes color.
At the zoo, a chameleon was sitting on a branch.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 카멜레온처럼 상황에 따라 변해요.
examples.en: That person changes like a chameleon depending on the situation.
My friend keeps a chameleon as a pet.
A chameleon's eyes move separately on each side.
He has a chameleon-like personality, so he's hard to trust.

explain: 동물 이름이지만 사람에게 쓰면 비유예요. 상황마다 태도를 바꾸는 사람을 '카멜레온 같다'고 말하는데, 칭찬보다는 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 카멜레온 같아서 누구 앞에서든 말이 달라져요.
phrases.en: to be like a chameleon (changing one's attitude to suit the situation)
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황이나 사람에 따라 태도와 말을 바꾸는 사람을 가리켜요. 약간 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who changes attitude and words depending on the situation or person. Slightly negative.

explain_en: It is an animal name, but used for a person it is a metaphor. People say '카멜레온 같다' about someone who changes attitude with each situation, which sounds slightly sarcastic rather than complimentary.

examples.en: A prism has a polygon as its base.
A triangular prism and a rectangular prism are both prisms.
We drew a prism in math class.
The side faces of a prism are rectangles.
This box is shaped like a prism.
How are a prism and a cylinder different?

explain: 수학에서 위아래 밑면이 같은 다각형인 기둥 모양 입체도형이에요. 밑면이 동그란 '원기둥', 뾰족한 '각뿔'과 같이 배워요. 일상에서는 '네모난 기둥'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: A triangular prism has triangular bases.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밑면 모양을 앞에 붙여 구체적인 각기둥 이름을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the base shape before the word to name a specific prism.

phrases.en: This box is shaped like a rectangular prism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 네모난 상자처럼 생긴 입체도형을 수학에서 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The math name for a box-like solid with square or rectangular bases.

phrases.en: A prism has two bases.
phrases.nuance_ko: '각기둥의 + 부분 이름'으로 수학 설명을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as 'prism's + part' when explaining the shape in math.

explain_en: Solid shape in math class with flat sides and two equal bases. In math it is a solid whose top and bottom bases are identical polygons. It is learned alongside the round-based '원기둥' (cylinder) and the pointed '각뿔' (pyramid). In daily life people say things like '네모난 기둥'.

t90.ax: We drew a prism in math class.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 강둑이 무너질까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so I'm worried the embankment might collapse.
I run along the riverbank every evening.
The cherry blossoms are in full bloom on the embankment.
Children fly kites on top of the embankment.
It takes ten minutes by bike to get to the embankment.

examples.ko: 강둑은 물이 넘치지 않게 막아 줘요.
examples.en: The embankment keeps the water from overflowing.

explain: 강물이 넘치지 않게 흙이나 돌로 쌓은 둑이에요. 자연스러운 물가인 '강기슭'과 달리 쌓아 올린 언덕이라서, 위에 산책로나 자전거길이 있는 곳이 많아요.

phrases.en: I ride a bike along the river embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둑 위의 산책로나 자전거길을 따라 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for moving along the path on top of an embankment.

phrases.en: The villagers built up the river embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 흙이나 돌로 만든 둑이라서 '쌓다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since it is made by people from soil or stone, 쌓다 fits well.

phrases.en: There is a bench on top of the embankment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓아 올린 언덕이라서 '위'와 함께 위치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is a raised bank, it pairs with 위 (on top) for location.

explain_en: Embankment along a river, to prevent flooding or to walk on. It is a bank built of earth or stone to keep a river from overflowing. Unlike '강기슭', the natural water's edge, it is a built-up ridge, and many have walking or bike paths on top.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 구김살 없이 밝게 자랐어요.
examples.en: That child grew up bright and carefree.
I smoothed the wrinkles out of my clothes with an iron.
I like her carefree smile.

examples.ko: 빨래를 널 때 구김살을 손으로 털어요.
examples.en: When hanging laundry, I shake out the wrinkles by hand.
Maybe because of worry, his face looked creased and tense.

examples.ko: 구김살 하나 없는 새 교복을 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore a brand-new school uniform without a single wrinkle.

explain: '구김'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만, '구김살 없다'처럼 마음이나 표정이 밝고 어두운 그늘이 없다는 뜻으로 더 자주 써요. 옷의 주름에는 '구김'이 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.example: 구김살 없이 자란 아이라서 누구한테나 친절해요.
phrases.en: He grew up carefree, so he's kind to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움이나 그늘 없이 밝고 자유롭게 자란 사람이나 표정을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It praises a person or expression that is bright and free of worry or hardship.

explain_en: Actual creases in cloth or paper; also dark shadow on face or mood (구김살 없다) It is nearly the same as '구김', but it is more often used in '구김살 없다' to describe a bright mind or face with no shadow. For clothes, '구김' sounds more everyday.

en: rim of the ear; area near the ear

examples.en: The wind brushed past my ear.
That song is still ringing in my ears.
My ear tickled, so I turned around.
Someone whispered softly right by my ear.
I pushed the hair by my ear behind it.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears turned red.

explain: 귀의 바로 옆을 말해요. '귓가에 맴돌다'는 들었던 소리나 말이 계속 들리는 듯한 느낌일 때 자주 써요. 소설이나 노래 가사에서도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: He whispered quietly beside my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀 바로 옆에서 작게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone speaks softly right next to your ear.

phrases.en: The sound of the bell still rings in my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 가까이에서 크게 들리거나 계속 들리는 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound seems close or keeps echoing.

phrases.en: That voice keeps lingering in my ears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들었던 소리나 말이 끝났는데도 계속 들리는 듯할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound or words you heard seem to keep playing after they ended.

explain_en: The place right next to the ear, where whispers or sounds are heard. It means the area right beside the ear. '귓가에 맴돌다' is often used when a sound or words you heard still seem to echo. It also appears a lot in novels and song lyrics.

examples.en: When I smile, the corners of my eyes turn down.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 눈꼬리에 선을 길게 그렸어요.
examples.en: When doing makeup, I drew a long line at the outer corner of my eye.
His eyes tilt up at the outer corners, so he looks a bit sharp.
As I got older, wrinkles appeared at the corners of my eyes.
My sibling's eyes droop at the corners, so they look gentle.
A makeup style that lifts the outer corners slightly is in fashion.

explain: 귀 쪽에 가까운 눈의 바깥쪽 끝이에요. 반대로 코 쪽 끝은 '눈머리'라고 해요. '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'로 인상을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My eyes turn up at the corners, so I look sharp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈의 모양으로 인상을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how eye shape affects someone's look.

phrases.en: Her eyes droop at the corners, so she looks gentle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올라가다'와 반대로 눈 끝이 아래로 내려갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 올라가다; the eye ends point down.

phrases.example: 눈머리는 코 쪽에 있고 눈꼬리는 귀 쪽에 있어요.
phrases.en: The inner corner is near the nose and the outer corner is near the ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈꼬리의 반대쪽, 코 쪽 끝을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The end of the eye near the nose, opposite of 눈꼬리.

explain_en: It is the outer end of the eye, near the ear. The end near the nose is '눈머리'. It is often used to describe someone's look, as in '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'.
